scope: Function contracts and named generated properties. A source-file association is not whole-file verification; direct test imports are not execution coverage.

propertyGroups.formalBoundary: The production receipt policy admits exact matches and only adopts missing receipts for permitted identities. Checked finite histories preserve accepted heads and keep a receiver's absent own receipt empty. Replacing a conflicting shorter head with an offered one after verifying the writer's signed suffix chain is runtime logic beside that policy, exercised by generated forged, truncated, reordered and tampered suffixes. Native tests cover signed and encrypted binding, detached CRDT merge, acknowledged journal publication, replay, context changes and restart. Trusted controller behavior, group membership and cryptographic secrecy remain separate assumptions.

The admitted-prefix proof composes the production count and byte reservation policy over any finite chunk stream. Runtime properties cover actual UnixFS exporter traversal, raw and chunked files, observed chunk lengths, aggregate charging, abort delivery and native AES authentication. Logical limits do not establish total browser memory, third-party parser work or wall-clock latency.

The production segment-prefix, grant and first-rejection selectors are exact. Checked composition proves prefix order, grant attenuation and that accepted finite target histories cannot overlap a protected path disjoint from every grant; rejected or stale batches contribute no targets. Inspection admission bounds scanned work, unique targets and retained string units. Native operation extraction is an explicit trusted abstraction, calibrated by actual Automerge object ancestry (including losing/deleted objects), Yjs integrated items before GC, forged origin references, raw deletion sets, predecessor-reference fuzzing and signed/encrypted document/WAL admission properties. Scalars, own descriptors, array ownership, native clocks/IDs, aggregate scope budgets and root/index lookup cost require properties. Native parser correctness, complete native heap/CPU bounds, hard browser scheduling, cryptographic unforgeability and the semantics of arbitrary application authority adapters are not proved. Field scopes apply to coordinated Automerge/Yjs mode, not the legacy BeeKEM/UCAN path.

Production retention-lease conjunction, candidate metadata admission and deletion phase transitions are verified. Exact finite transition histories prove at most one deletion entry per attempt and no entry when all observations deny a live unpinned lease. Native properties check the actual document mutation queue across pin and delete awaits, a lease captured again after a stale tree or snapshot, an edit between every deletion slot, one attempt per candidate per pass, existing pins, coalescing, atomic metadata refusal, close quiescence, provider failures described without trusting the thrown value, and explicit retry. The offline Helia fixture uses actual CIDs, pinning and blockstore deletion. Native pointer/Set ownership, truthful pin observations, provider I/O completion, Helia locks, persistence, global storage quotas, VM heap and UI latency remain assumptions or integration boundaries.

The actual deletion selector has exact candidate/retained/protected membership. Checked composition proves that adding protections can only reduce deletions, partitioned batches have the same selected union, and arbitrary finite sweep histories preserve initially retained/protected and unrelated blocks under fixed truthful guard sets. Native properties call the actual document pruner and GC adapter to check ACL payload preservation, sparse aliases, rejection before publishing malformed trees, owned selection results and per-occurrence reflection counts through the node cap. CID parsing is stubbed in these properties; cryptographic authentication, dynamic guard freshness, asynchronous blockstore deletion, crash durability, native heap and UI latency are not proved.

Known-change trimming has no formal proof. Generated finite histories of changes, unknown references, redeliveries and trims check the production trim rule against an exact model: current-generation entries survive, previous-generation hashes survive only when retained, previous-generation referenced ancestors survive when retained or still known, and the frontier is unchanged whenever every head is retained; retention keeps at most one generation of the newest heads. Document tests drive the real change, sync, load and checkpoint paths. Redelivery of a change older than the window, CRDT merge idempotence, CID parsing, cryptographic authentication and checkpoint storage are outside these properties.

The actual store policies check exact staged revision/count/byte admission, unique bounded publication append/removal with exact byte totals and retained-index projection, and token/checkpoint-bound commit eligibility. Checked finite histories preserve metadata bounds and leave accepted entries unchanged on failed/rejected operations; histories without checkpoint commits retain the initial accepted prefix. Native strict scalar guards, byte equality, owned record/payload projection, pending checkpoint retention, transaction aborts and authenticated encrypted recovery require properties. Storage success and payload-match truth are model inputs; crash durability, cryptographic unforgeability, browser quota behavior and UI latency are not proved.

The actual history index and consuming traversal prove rooted, distinct predecessor order, exact acceptance of complete append chains, fork/orphan rejection and at most N+1 successor probes for at most 1000 items. Tail clocks have checked exact safe-integer bounds. Native Map/Set lookup, array ownership, IEEE-754 arithmetic, Yjs item encoding and batched actor histories require properties. Native read counters reproduce and prevent quadratic predecessor scans. These are abstract traversal-work and local validation guarantees; Yjs codecs, hash-table cost, cryptographic authentication, arbitrary concurrent epoch recovery, native heap use and UI latency remain outside the proof.

The actual UTF-8 sizing implementation has checked exact prefix-weight accounting, accepts exactly paired UTF-16 whose UTF-8 weight fits the byte cap, and returns its exact byte count. Rejected excessive code-unit lengths perform no scan; admitted scans have a decreasing variant bounded by the configured byte cap. Native TextEncoder semantics, string access counts, safe-integer/type guards, metadata validation before graph/payload work, canonical hash/signature bytes and input mutation across digest yields require properties. These are scalar/loop-work guarantees, not a proof of VM heap usage, wall-clock/UI latency, cryptographic unforgeability or the complete asynchronous load protocol.
Native IEEE-754 arithmetic, data views, UTF-16 operations and frozen exports remain trusted runtime boundaries.

All supported tree indices, parent/child identities and bounded ragged-tree paths are proved. Native integer guards, exact power lookup and JavaScript execution are calibrated with independent BigInt/binary oracles.

The exact-next parent and writer guard, same-generation competing public tree decision, existing-leaf non-reactivation, and optional checkpoint commitment matching are proved. Finite histories preserve accepted generation and revoked slots with an authenticated checkpoint and an independently trusted current pin. Native tree construction, WebCrypto keys, removal and fork paths, recipient access, export and restoration require generated tests. This does not establish distributed ACL revocation, durable fork quarantine, forward secrecy or post-compromise security.

The production phase, revision, owner and stop guard is exact. Finite histories keep quarantine absorbing, prevent stale or foreign release and keep an active record fenced after an interrupted stop. Seeded runtime schedules check competing acquisitions, scope separation, close during acquisition and before/after-write interruptions. Process and Yjs fixtures check restart and refusal to restore a valid pinned checkpoint after a local authenticated fork. The guarantees depend on an independent exact durable CAS, a fresh lease and authenticated local fork detection. An application store's durability and group-wide fork resolution remain outside this evidence.

Proved document admission budgets bound count and byte reservations across finite histories. The runtime applies one budget to the PubSub listener and validator per subscription and a second budget across the module. Native properties check detached ownership, admission across multiple scopes, pending work at close, and signature batching. The accounting covers admitted ciphertext bytes and work items. Heap overhead, peer scheduling, native CPU and recovery of locally skipped messages remain outside the proof.

The field-path selector finds the first complete marker in the final line with a nonempty suffix. Its backward and forward scans each visit at most the input length. Native UTF-16 code units, JSON and reflection, typed arrays, aliases and chunked async input require runtime calibration.
Mutable maps, WeakRef ownership, deferred finalizers and native byte storage are not established by the pure admission proofs.

Checked production budget, pressure, projection and insertion helpers compose into bounded finite histories. Unverified admission preserves authenticated metadata and value bindings, exact byte accounting and immutable rejected states. Header admission is monotone in body size. The model assumes correct authentication flags, bounded detached metadata and owned input maps; native strict flags/keys, byte lengths and buffer ownership, serializer reentrancy, injected preparation failures, BigInt arithmetic and native Map/array identity require properties. This is a per-buffer resource and retention proof, not a signature, durable-delivery or UI-latency guarantee.

Checked expiry membership, exact retained bytes and a nondecreasing sampled clock compose with admission, removal and opaque value projection into finite histories. Failed preparations and rejected stores preserve the clock; retained receipt times are bounded by it, and successful pruning removes exactly entries whose observed age exceeds the TTL. Native safe-integer arithmetic, array/Map ownership, injected preparation failures, malformed clocks and the actual replay drain require properties. Authentication and scheduling remain assumptions; this does not prove a wall-clock deadline, periodic pruning, arbitrary-schedule replay safety or UI latency.

Sequential partition, revision, epoch, byte-budget and claim laws are proved. Promise scheduling, failures, callback side effects, rollback and native encrypted-envelope ownership require generated execution histories.
Native signing/encryption and asynchronous delegation verification are outside the proof; integrity checks do not prove cryptographic secrecy or unforgeability.
Third-party CRDT engines, native serialization and out-of-order delivery are outside the proof model.

Scalar order, lexicographic order composition, prefix-page reconstruction and reserved field segment exclusion are proved within the model. Native IEEE-754/UTF-16 correspondence, own-data field extraction, projection branch ownership, JSON cursors, index planning and IndexedDB require runtime properties.
IEEE-754/int32 hashing and bitwise operations are outside the pinned model; generated merge laws and no-false-negative checks do not prove a false-positive probability.
JavaScript object identity, WeakMap ownership, prototype semantics and immutable Redux updates require runtime state histories.
Counter mutation and finite floating-point byte inputs are outside the integer-only functional proof.

The bounded retry admission decision is proved. Native transport error classification, asynchronous failure schedules, AbortSignal cancellation and diagnostic observer isolation remain runtime boundaries.

Least graph reachability, edge-linear queue bounds and ACL pruning admission are proved for detached nodes and edges. Heap traversal, CID aliases, object snapshots and descendant ACL preservation remain runtime boundaries.

Atomic reservation, exact membership append admission and uint64 epoch sequence laws are proved. Native signature verification, authority lookup, shared mutable budgets, asynchronous queues, callback failures, cancellation, fork latching and byte ownership still require generated execution histories.

Field range/trailer separation and bounded chunk-copy progress are proved. DataView endianness, native safe-integer arithmetic, typed-array offsets, Uint8ArrayList chunks, stream cleanup, canonical decoding and ownership require native malformed-input and model-calibration properties.

The production field-write planner accepts exactly when the payload and complete four-byte prefix, if present, fit both field and writer limits. Rejection preserves the offset and retains no payload or parts; accepted fields account for exactly one owned payload copy and omit empty parts. Checked arbitrary finite histories, with native-copy success as an input, bound retained payload bytes and part counts by the encoded byte budget and preserve exact payload/prefix accounting. Native safe-integer guards, actual typed-array copies, prefix endianness, malformed/shared/detached views, field ownership and failure before commit require properties. Native representation calibration inspects retained parts to establish the planner's resource assumptions. The model does not bound transient allocations, output materialization, TextEncoder work, VM heap overhead, UI latency or cryptographic security.

Exact first-eligible identity selection, digest multiplicities, strict-majority uniqueness, stable cohort projection and failure precedence are proved. Native bytes and map iteration, authority attribution, reflected probe results, Promise completion order, caller mutation and private error handling require runtime properties. Probe signatures and authorizer correctness remain caller responsibilities.

Production reservation and phase transitions have checked contracts and unbounded finite-history accounting/commit laws requiring both matching context and authorization. Promise cancellation, byte ownership, exact native closure accounting, protected anchor freshness, current-authorization guards, preparation/finalizer contracts and queue isolation remain runtime boundaries. Authentication and causal role authorization are trusted preparation obligations; this is not a whole-document or cryptographic secrecy proof.

The common stage lifecycle proves successful completion only after application succeeds and failed applications cannot be retried. Runtime callbacks and exact cleanup invocation still require calibration. Automerge immutable cloning, native missing-dependency detection, recursive callbacks, Yjs scalar/shared-type payload restrictions, escaped references, checkpoint merge/discard and constant-actor reuse require native generated execution histories.

Requests carry receipts in the same canonical receipt codec and resent frames re-enter the proved sequence policy. Request framing, the GossipSub sender binding, replay and per-member intervals, the shared resend budget, suffix completeness and suppression are runtime state over network timing, so generated encodings and native scenarios exercise them. Real GossipSub delivery, peer scoring and traffic analysis remain outside these checks.

Topic requests carry receipts in the same canonical receipt codec, and their checkpoints are merged through the same proved receipt admission and runtime suffix verification as relayed checkpoints. Request and checkpoint framing, the separate encryption domains, the GossipSub sender binding, issue-time freshness and replay, controller-only answers, the application authorization callback, signed refusals, the oversized-snapshot cache, the per-member interval, the per-document share of the process checkpoint budget, outstanding challenges, triggers and backoff are runtime state over network timing, so generated encodings and native scenarios exercise them. Real GossipSub delivery, clock skew between members, peer scoring and traffic analysis remain outside these checks.

The production sequence policy still classifies each frame as apply, replay, gap or parent mismatch. A gap or a native missing-dependency error after full authentication holds the frame instead of rejecting it, and a held frame is admitted later only through the same proved policy. The hold bounds, per-author shares, eviction, expiry, equivocation check, dependency-targeted retry, release order and context reset are runtime state over arbitrary arrival orders, and native Automerge and Yjs dependency detection and naming is adapter behavior, so generated arrival orders and focused bound, retry-cost and session tests exercise them. Network delivery and redelivery of frames that never arrive remain outside these checks.

The proved journal recovery classifier and anchor policies are unchanged: a divergence marker is one more authenticated, chained entry, so dropping it reads as a rollback through the same anchor decision. That the marker ends the accepted branch, that a marker carries no content, and that every non-checkpoint entry carries a bounded path list are runtime decoding rules, exercised with sealed malformed, flipped, replayed and trailing entries on both stores. Exactness of the recorded paths, that grants cover the record exactly when they cover every inspected path, is checked by generated paths and grants against the proved prefix-grant policy. Deleting a diverged journal is a store transaction checked on both stores. Native operation inspection, its bounds and CRDT dependency order remain adapter behavior.

Sequence, role, epoch advancement, journal recovery, publication-ledger insertion/projection, durable selection, finite-history provenance and exact bounded roster equality are proved. Native checks exercise authority changes during journal reads, delayed identity checks, malformed provider rosters, ownership of recovered paths and authenticated group revocation across restart. Native Map aliasing, detached candidates, encrypted receipts, provider signatures/exporters, CRDT parsing, signed roster ownership, IndexedDB transactions, mixed crash histories and rollback-anchor conformance also require runtime checks. Cryptographic primitives, network liveness and secure hardware storage remain outside these checks.

The production read planner preserves every accepted-entry request, suppresses pending/outbox body reads in recovery mode, retains exactly a discard token and accounts for each planned row get. Checked composition with the actual recovery classifier gates later outbox reads on authenticated state and a successful required anchor decision, requires a matching final anchor observation before exposing recovered state, derives a 147-row get bound and saves one body read per queued publication and pending entry. These are IndexedDB journal get counts, excluding anchor-provider I/O, writes and cryptographic costs. Native transaction scopes, field/buffer ownership, optional capability dispatch, actual crypto/anchor checks and post-await mutation require properties. The proof assumes truthful validation/anchor observations; it does not prove signatures, browser heap use, storage durability or UI latency.

The retained revision index accepts exactly bounded contiguous suffixes ending at the stored head with coherent minimum byte counts. Production boundedFieldEnd decisions guard native row copies; checked arbitrary finite read histories preserve exact admitted-byte sums within the declared budget, exclude zero-length copies, keep failed preparations unchanged and make failure absorbing. A batch corollary bounds accepted rows by 128. Native safe-integer guards, IndexedDB transaction/abort behavior, structured cloning, ciphertext ownership, byte-copy instrumentation and mutation during anchor awaits require properties. The proof does not bound browser structured-clone allocations, decoding buffers, total heap use or UI latency, and does not establish cryptographic authenticity or rollback-anchor honesty.

Detached roster acceptance is proved iff every entry has valid scalar fields, identities are unique and the local member exists. Successful lookup maps contain exactly the original ID/key/role bindings, retain at most 256 entries and expose no partial map on rejection. The immutable record/map model assumes owned scalar inputs. Native own-data descriptors, bounded indexed arrays, intrinsic byte copies, map independence, receiver-bound callback capture and asynchronous authorization invalidation require properties. Truthful synchronous provider guards, proxy behavior, cryptographic validity and UI latency are outside this proof; provider-boundary counterexamples are not evidence of a remote exploit.

Exact roster shape, role validity, unique identities/keys, single-controller selection and fresh bounded controller binding are proved. Checked finite histories preserve every historical controller and admit a valid signed first transition. Native Map and byte ownership, numeric calibration, canonical wire parsing, Ed25519 signatures and racing asynchronous role updates require runtime properties. A signedByCurrent proof input assumes correct authentication; cryptographic unforgeability and provider membership are not established.

Exact conflict classification, join/acceptance/index transitions, expiry projection, monotone clock and sweep frontier are proved. Checked arbitrary finite histories preserve signed join and consumed-acceptance bindings, prevent revival after expiry and bound each of four indexes by capacity. The model assumes a fixed digest-to-offer catalog, truthful validation and distinct owned maps. Native in-place Map identity, record/array ownership, canonical wire snapshots, actual SHA/signature binding, malformed clocks, immutable capacity and asynchronous digest schedules require properties. Signature verification is the caller's responsibility. This is per-instance replay memory, not a cryptographic secrecy, durable-replay or UI-latency proof; expiry sweeps remain linear in capacity.

Timestamp-window classification, monotone clock observation, exact replay retirement, immutable bounded replay admission and response eligibility are proved. A finite-history model preserves live nonces and establishes 46 retained response attempts from empty state under the 60-second lifetime, 30-second future skew and 2-second spacing. Native Map identity, signed JSON/CID framing, crypto callbacks, clock validity, post-authentication and dispatch freshness, publication failures, callback authorization and registered GossipSub verdicts independent of local response history require runtime properties. This does not prove provider correctness, UI latency, arbitrary callback liveness or durable replay protection across process restarts.

No scheduler contract is proved. Generated signal histories with fake time check that at most one timer is armed, requests stay at least the minimum interval apart, quiet periods are never longer than four thirds of the periodic interval, loads stay a load interval apart, follow a request by the load delay and target only connected writer advertisers, and nothing loads without the commitment resolver. Real timers, the shared budget across documents, signature verification of advertisements and the authenticated load itself are covered by example, native and real-node tests; network delivery, UI latency and many-peer traffic are outside this evidence.

Carrying a delivered remote tip inline has no formal proof. Generated pairs of retained and delivered trees over one acyclic history, with aliases, sparse citations and pruned or content-stripped descriptions, check that the merged change passes the production alias validator, that the copy describes no CID the retained tree already describes, that every delivered change reachable without passing a described CID stays inline, and that the copy cites without content only described or kept CIDs. Which blocks a replica stores, the frame budget, signature and actor checks, CID parsing and the network are covered by example and real-node tests or remain outside this evidence.

The production locator classification and staged publication gate are exact. Finite histories from one pinned base prove monotone revision, at most one accepted successor and that it comes from an approved, content-matching, staged CAS attempt. Native checks cover bounded ownership, authorization and hashing, delayed preparation, distinct and identical concurrent preparations, and restart after interrupted staging or acknowledgment. The Yjs fixture reopens a fresh checkpoint and verifies selected content and a fresh epoch. The model trusts the application approval, private durable staging and independently protected atomic locator, and does not provide distributed branch selection, peer-assisted recovery, or browser storage durability.

Generated hold and release sequences check the held ACL change buffer directly: every per-signer and per-document count and byte bound holds after each step, a change leaves only by release or by an eviction the buffer reports, re-holding a change refreshes it without counting it twice, and eviction takes the offending signer's oldest change, or past the document bound the oldest change of the signer holding the most. Whether a held change's missing dependencies have arrived is decided by each ACL adapter's ready() check, which native Yjs and Automerge dependency tests calibrate; the buffer does not prove that check, signer authentication, merge order or CRDT convergence, and no policy file models it.

integrationBoundaries.boundary: Local BeeKEM fork quarantine with persistence, process restart and native pinned checkpoint admission
Explicit application recovery through a staged fresh document, pinned checkpoint and separate locator
WebRTC/libp2p, NAT/relay behavior, transport loss and browser limits
Real browser storage, restart, eviction and UI scheduling
Closing documents while they open, live block GC during continuous edits with and without a content router, and default GossipSub IP scoring on loopback libp2p TCP nodes
Packed module loading, API declarations and reference applications
Malformed-input attacks, proxy/getter behavior, cancellation and cryptographic protocol assumptions not covered by a named contract/property

remainingLimits: No whole-product proof or semantic coverage percentage is claimed.
Native cryptographic entropy remains native; generated data and operation schedules have fixed seeds.
The proofs do not establish caller authentication, cryptographic secrecy, durable storage, arbitrary scheduler liveness or browser resource budgets.
Known capability gaps reported by diagnostic scenarios remain gaps.
